quizName:
DMV Practice Test  #14
										  					
  

36 Questions • Passing Score 30

questions.question: What does this road sign mean?

options.text: Do not enter.
Roundabout ahead.
No U-turns.

questions.correctAnswerText: No U-turns.
questions.explanation: This is a regulatory sign. It tells drivers that making a U-turn is not allowed.

questions.question: A large truck is turning right onto a street with two lanes in each direction. What might the truck do?

options.text: May complete its turn in either of the two lanes.
May have to swing wide to complete the right turn.
Must stay in the right lane at all times while turning.

questions.correctAnswerText: May have to swing wide to complete the right turn.
questions.explanation: When turning, the rear wheels follow a shorter path than the front wheels. Long trucks need extra space to turn right, so they may swing wide to complete the turn.

questions.question: When changing lanes, which action should you never do?

options.text: Look over your shoulder to check your blind spot.
Change lanes abruptly or without warning.
Check for other vehicles moving into the same lane.

questions.correctAnswerText: Change lanes abruptly or without warning.
questions.explanation: When changing lanes, check your mirrors and blind spots first. Use your turn signal before changing lanes to warn other drivers. Never change lanes suddenly.

questions.question: When can you cross a double yellow line to pass another vehicle?

options.text: When the yellow line on the other side is solid.
When the yellow line on your side is broken.
When the yellow line on the other side is broken.

questions.correctAnswerText: When the yellow line on your side is broken.
questions.explanation: You can pass if a broken yellow line is next to your driving lane.

questions.question: How can you check your blind spot when changing lanes?

options.text: Use the inside rearview mirror.
Turn your head and look over your shoulder.
Use your side mirror.

questions.correctAnswerText: Turn your head and look over your shoulder.
questions.explanation: Mirrors cannot show all blind spots. Always look over your shoulder before changing lanes.

questions.question: What is true about vehicles with hazardous load signs?

options.text: They are not allowed on freeways.
They must stop before crossing railroad tracks.
They cannot exceed 35 mph.

questions.correctAnswerText: They must stop before crossing railroad tracks.
questions.explanation: Vehicles carrying hazardous materials must come to a complete stop before crossing railroad tracks.

questions.question: What does this yellow sign mean?

options.text: One lane ahead.
Merging traffic ahead.
Lane ends ahead.

questions.correctAnswerText: Merging traffic ahead.
questions.explanation: This sign warns you that traffic may merge into your lane ahead.

questions.question: If your vehicle's rear is skidding to the left, what should you do?

options.text: Do not turn your steering wheel.
Turn your steering wheel to the left to correct the skid.
Turn your steering wheel to the right to correct the skid.

questions.correctAnswerText: Turn your steering wheel to the left to correct the skid.
questions.explanation: If you skid, turn your steering wheel in the direction the rear is sliding. Take your foot off the gas and avoid using the brakes. If you have anti-lock brakes, press firmly on the brakes and steer straight.

questions.question: For drivers 21 and older, it is illegal to drive with a blood alcohol concentration (BAC) of ____ or higher.

options.text: 0.08% (eight-hundredths of one percent)
0.10% (one-tenth of one percent)
0.05% (five-hundredths of one percent)

questions.correctAnswerText: 0.08% (eight-hundredths of one percent)
questions.explanation: For drivers 21 and older, it is illegal to drive with a BAC of 0.08% or higher. Drinking and driving is illegal and dangerous.

questions.question: When using a roundabout, what should drivers do?

options.text: Stop in the middle of the roundabout.
Yield to traffic already in the roundabout.
Yield to entering traffic.

questions.correctAnswerText: Yield to traffic already in the roundabout.
questions.explanation: A roundabout is a circular intersection with no traffic signal. Traffic flows counterclockwise around a center island. Enter from the right, yield to traffic already in the roundabout, and stay in the circle until you reach your exit.

questions.question: If you feel drowsy while driving, what should you do?

options.text: Try to stay awake.
Take a break.
Take caffeine pills.

questions.correctAnswerText: Take a break.
questions.explanation: If you feel tired, pull over at a rest stop and take a nap, stretch, or let someone else drive. Caffeine pills are not a safe substitute for real rest.

questions.question: Your reaction time is slower after:

options.text: Drinking alcohol.
Sleeping.
Working hard.

questions.correctAnswerText: Drinking alcohol.
questions.explanation: Alcohol slows your reflexes and reaction time. It reduces your vision and alertness. As you drink more, your judgment worsens and your driving skills decrease. You will have trouble judging distances and speeds.

questions.question: When you see an emergency vehicle with flashing lights approaching, what must you do?

options.text: Keep your speed and stay in your lane until it passes.
Move to the right lane and drive slowly until it passes.
Pull over to the edge of the road and stop until it passes.

questions.correctAnswerText: Pull over to the edge of the road and stop until it passes.
questions.explanation: When you see an emergency vehicle with flashing lights, pull to the right edge of the road and stop. Position your vehicle parallel to the curb. On one-way streets, move toward the nearest road edge.

questions.question: You want to park uphill on a two-way road with no curb. Which way should you turn your front wheels?

options.text: Straight ahead
Right, toward the side of the road
Left, toward the center of the road

questions.correctAnswerText: Right, toward the side of the road
questions.explanation: When parking uphill or downhill on a road with no curb, turn your wheels toward the side of the road. This way, if your brakes fail, your car will roll away from traffic.

questions.question: When bad weather makes it hard to see, what should you do?

options.text: Speed up to get off the road quickly.
Drive in the lane closest to oncoming traffic.
Increase your following distance.

questions.correctAnswerText: Increase your following distance.
questions.explanation: In darkness or poor weather, increase the distance between your car and the car ahead. This gives you more time to react to hazards you may not see.

questions.question: What is true about bridges and overpasses in cold, wet weather?

options.text: They freeze before the rest of the road.
They do not freeze because they are made of concrete.
They freeze after the rest of the road.

questions.correctAnswerText: They freeze before the rest of the road.
questions.explanation: Bridges and overpasses freeze before the rest of the road. They can have hidden ice patches.

questions.question: When passing another vehicle on the left, when is it safe to move back to the right lane?

options.text: After about three seconds.
When you can no longer see the vehicle over your right shoulder.
When you can see the front of the vehicle in your rearview mirror.

questions.correctAnswerText: When you can see the front of the vehicle in your rearview mirror.
questions.explanation: You can move back to the right lane when you can see the headlights of the passed vehicle in your rearview mirror. Always signal before changing lanes.

questions.question: Never make a U-turn:

options.text: in residential neighborhoods.
at or on a railroad crossing.
where there is no "No U-turn" sign.

questions.correctAnswerText: at or on a railroad crossing.
questions.explanation: Never make a U-turn at or on a railroad crossing, on a divided highway, when you cannot see clearly for 200 feet in each direction, on a one-way street, or in front of a fire station. Also avoid U-turns in business districts where they are prohibited.

questions.question: When should drivers yield the right-of-way to pedestrians in a crosswalk?

options.text: Only if the pedestrians wave to the driver first.
Only if the pedestrians are not texting while walking.
At all times.

questions.correctAnswerText: At all times.
questions.explanation: Stop your vehicle at a crosswalk to let any pedestrian cross. You may go slowly only if your lane is completely clear.

questions.question: It is illegal to park your vehicle:

options.text: In an unmarked crosswalk.
Within three feet of a private driveway.
In a bicycle lane.

questions.correctAnswerText: In an unmarked crosswalk.
questions.explanation: You cannot park in a marked or unmarked crosswalk. You can park in a bicycle lane only if there is no "No parking" sign and your car does not block bicyclists.

questions.question: Work zone barriers, drums, cones, and signs are used to:

options.text: Make drivers angry about slow traffic.
Inconvenience drivers.
Keep traffic out of dangerous work areas.

questions.correctAnswerText: Keep traffic out of dangerous work areas.
questions.explanation: Work zones are dangerous for both workers and drivers. Watch for cones, barrels, signs, large vehicles, and workers in bright vests. They warn you and show you where to go.

questions.question: It is illegal to leave a child age six or younger alone in a vehicle:

options.text: Even if they are in a child safety seat.
If they are with someone age twelve or older.
Only if the keys are in the ignition.

questions.correctAnswerText: Even if they are in a child safety seat.
questions.explanation: Never leave a child age six or younger alone in a car. A child may be left with someone age twelve or older.

questions.question: To avoid hydroplaning in rain, you should:

options.text: Drive at a speed that works for good weather.
Use your brakes as soon as your car starts to skid.
Slow down.

questions.correctAnswerText: Slow down.
questions.explanation: Driving too fast in wet conditions causes your tires to lose grip with the road. Your car will ride on top of the water, which is called hydroplaning. Driving slowly in rain prevents this.

questions.question: What is the benefit of leaving space around your vehicle?

options.text: Other drivers can cut in front of you, which helps traffic flow.
You have time to react if another driver makes a mistake.
It protects you from injury during a crash.

questions.correctAnswerText: You have time to react if another driver makes a mistake.
questions.explanation: Space around your vehicle gives you time to safely react to another driver's mistake. For example, you may have time to brake or steer away if a car moves into your lane.

questions.question: A white painted curb means:

options.text: A loading zone for freight or passengers.
A loading zone for passengers or mail only.
A loading zone for freight only.

questions.correctAnswerText: A loading zone for passengers or mail only.
questions.explanation: At a white curb, you may stop only to pick up or drop off passengers or mail.

questions.question: To avoid skidding on slippery surfaces, you should:

options.text: Shift to a lower gear after starting down a steep hill.
Speed up to enter curves and slow down to exit them.
Slow down before entering curves and intersections.

questions.correctAnswerText: Slow down before entering curves and intersections.
questions.explanation: Slow down before you enter a curve because you do not know what is ahead. Braking in a curve may cause you to skid.

questions.question: This yellow sign means:

options.text: There is a sharp turn to the right.
You must turn right.
You can only turn right on a green arrow.

questions.correctAnswerText: There is a sharp turn to the right.
questions.explanation: Yellow signs warn of upcoming road conditions like curves and sharp turns.

questions.question: A blood alcohol level of 0.02 percent:

options.text: Will not affect your driving.
Will not put other drivers at risk.
Will double your chances of having an accident.

questions.correctAnswerText: Will double your chances of having an accident.
questions.explanation: Each 0.02 percent increase in blood alcohol nearly doubles your risk of a fatal crash.

questions.question: Motorcycles, scooters, and mopeds are hard to see. You should:

options.text: Slow down when driving.
Check your mirrors and blind spots often.
Share a lane with a motorcycle.

questions.correctAnswerText: Check your mirrors and blind spots often.
questions.explanation: Motorcycles can hide in your blind spot or be missed because they are small. Always look carefully for motorcycles, mopeds, and scooters.

questions.question: You hit a parked car and cannot find the owner. What should you do?

options.text: Call your insurance company when you get home.
Wait for the owner to return.
Leave a note with your name and address on the car.

questions.correctAnswerText: Leave a note with your name and address on the car.
questions.explanation: If you hit a parked car or property, you must leave a note with your name, phone number, and address on the vehicle or property.

questions.question: A broken yellow centerline means:

options.text: Passing is not allowed.
You can pass on the right when the road is clear.
You can pass on the left when the road is clear.

questions.correctAnswerText: You can pass on the left when the road is clear.
questions.explanation: A broken yellow line on your side means you can cross the line to pass other cars.

questions.question: A broken yellow line next to a solid yellow line means:

options.text: Passing is allowed from the lane with the solid yellow line.
Passing is not allowed from either direction.
Passing is allowed from the lane with the broken yellow line.

questions.correctAnswerText: Passing is allowed from the lane with the broken yellow line.
questions.explanation: The broken line side can pass. The solid line side cannot pass.

questions.question: When entering an interstate, you should:

options.text: Stop, check for cars, and enter when safe.
Check for cars and slow to 25 mph before entering the lane.
Check for cars, speed up to match traffic, and merge when clear.

questions.correctAnswerText: Check for cars, speed up to match traffic, and merge when clear.
questions.explanation: Use the merge lane to speed up and smoothly join traffic already on the interstate. Do not stop.

questions.question: This road sign means:

options.text: Drive carefully and be ready to stop.
You must come to a complete stop.
Stop only if needed.

questions.correctAnswerText: You must come to a complete stop.
questions.explanation: The stop sign is the only eight-sided sign on roads. You must stop completely and may not go until the way is clear.

questions.question: When a car with bright headlights drives toward you at night, you should:

options.text: Stop until the other car passes.
Look below their headlights.
Look toward the right edge of your lane.

questions.correctAnswerText: Look toward the right edge of your lane.
questions.explanation: Do not look directly at oncoming headlights at night. Instead, look toward the right edge of the road until the car passes.

questions.question: Roads are most slippery:

options.text: During heavy rain.
After it has been raining for a while.
During the first rain after a dry period.

questions.correctAnswerText: During the first rain after a dry period.
questions.explanation: Roads are most slippery during the first rain after a dry time because oil and dust have not been washed away yet.
